cards.explanation: The answer is twelve. Luke says that when He was twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the Feast (Luke 2:42). So this trip is the same yearly trip, just with a twelve-year-old along. I bet the family packed the same way they always did.

The answer is False. Luke says the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed (Luke 2:43). They set off for home with no idea. I've lost track of a cookie or two on the cooling rack, friends, but never a whole twelve-year-old!

The answer is among their relatives and friends. Luke says they traveled on for a day before they began to look for Him among their relatives and friends (Luke 2:44). They had been assuming He was in their company. So they started with the people they knew.

The answer is that they went back to Jerusalem to search. Luke says that when they could not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem to search for Him (Luke 2:45). They didn't give up on Him, friends. That tells you plenty.
The answer is three. Luke says that finally, after three days, they found Him (Luke 2:46). The word finally is right there in the verse. I think every one of those days felt long to them.

The answer is the temple courts. Luke says they found Him there, sitting among the teachers (Luke 2:46). I once tore my whole bakery apart looking for my chef's hat, and it was on my head the entire time. Their search ended with a far bigger surprise than mine.

The answer is listening and asking them questions. Luke says He was sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions (Luke 2:46). Nothing in this verse says He was lecturing. And yet the next verse says all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers (Luke 2:47).
The answer is astounded. Luke says that all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers (Luke 2:47). Notice it says all, friends, not some.

The answer is in His Father's house. Jesus asks, “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house?” (Luke 2:49). His mother had just told Him they'd been anxiously searching, and He answers with a question of His own. Luke says they did not understand the statement He was making to them (Luke 2:50).

The answer is False. Luke says, “But they did not understand the statement He was making to them.” (Luke 2:50). Jesus was saying it right to them, and it still didn't click. I've nodded along to plenty of directions I didn't follow, so I get it.

The answer is True. Luke says that Jesus went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them (Luke 2:51). This is the same boy who just astounded the teachers (Luke 2:47). He goes home and is obedient to His parents.

The answer is treasures. Luke says, “…treasured up all these things in her heart.” (Luke 2:51). Treasured is the word Luke uses for what she did with them. I think it's the way you'd hold onto your favorite recipe card.

The answer is both God and man. Luke says that Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man (Luke 2:52). He grew in how He was seen by God and by people. That's how this story ends.
